blocks.heading: Price
blocks.text: Price is the monetary value that you pay for something or that something costs. For the customer it is part of the sacrifice made to obtain the offering; for the seller it affects revenue and the surplus after costs. Price interacts with perceived quality, competition, affordability and demand. A higher price can increase revenue per unit while reducing quantity sold; a lower price can increase volume without necessarily increasing profit. Distinguish the price paid by the customer from the producer’s cost of making the item.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Kena Bags sells a bag for N$150 although its stated unit cost is N$100. N$150 is price and N$100 is cost. The N$50 difference over that stated cost is not evidence that every future price rise would be profitable.
